title: Nsight GPU occupancy + utilization run notes (Feb 2026)
content:
Purpose:
Quick notes from Nsight Systems + Nsight Compute runs focused on GPU occupancy and utilization for the v1.12 attention + kv-cache hot path. Goal: explain where cycles are being lost (low SM occupancy vs memory-bound kernels vs kernel launch overhead), validate CUDA Graphs impact, and propose concrete follow-ups.

Context / setup:
- Model: opt-6.7b FP16 (custom fused attention kernels in main branch)
- Hardware: p4d.24xlarge equivalent (A100 80GB) used for controlled runs
- Workload: inference single-stream synchronous serving with batch size 1 and dynamic padding; typical seq_len=512, prompt length range 64-512.
- Commands: nsight-sys and nsight-compute runs collected on same workload. Example capture: 
  nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt -o nsight_run_20260225 ./serve --model opt-6.7b --profile-run 
  nsight-cu-cli --metrics sm__warps_active.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_active,sm__cycles_active.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_active,dram__throughput.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_elapsed kernel_name

High-level findings:
1) Overall GPU utilization (SM active cycles) is ~45% for seq_len 512 single-stream requests. Utilization increases to ~70-75% when batching 4x.
2) Peak occupancy (per-kernel reported by Nsight Compute) varies widely: attention forward kernels show theoretical occupancy 40-55% (occupancy limited by registers and shared memory), softmax and gelu kernels show very low occupancy (~20-30%) due to small thread blocks and memory-bound ops.
3) Significant gaps between kernel launches: timeline shows many short-lived kernels (~20-200us) with gaps (host-side latency) between launches; small kernels + launch overhead accounts for ~12-18% of total timeline idle time.
4) CUDA Graphs reproduction: building CUDA Graphs for the token-generation loop reduces CPU->GPU launch stalls and improves measured SM utilization by ~8-10% and reduces 99p latency by ~10%.

Detailed timeline notes:
- Kernel timeline snapshot (seq=512, bs=1):
  - kv-cache load kernels: multiple small memcpy-ish kernels (H2D/D2H avoided because memory is GPU-resident) -- these are fine but spawn many small kernels for chunked copies (look into coalescing).
  - attention-matmul (fused) kernels: long-running (~1.2ms) but only ~50% occupancy. Nsight compute suggests register pressure is high (per-thread register usage forces fewer active warps).
  - softmax-reduction kernels: short (~60-180us), memory-bound; DRAM throughput near 40-55% of peak for these ops.
  - output-projection + layer-norm: mixed-bound, ~200-400us, occupancy 35-60% depending on sequence slice.
  - post-processing host-side steps (prompt tokenization, logging) occasionally cause 300-600us CPU-side gaps in the timeline; these should be offloaded or precomputed in hot path.

Nsight Compute metric highlights (avg across hot kernels):
- sm__warps_active.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_active: 42-52% (attention fused kernels)
- sm__cycles_active.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_active: 45% overall
- achieved_occupancy: 0.38-0.56 depending on kernel
- dram__throughput.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_elapsed: 28-60% (softmax/gelu higher, matmuls lower due to cache reuse)
- inst_executed: high integer/logic ops in softmax reduction kernels (branch divergence observed in some warps)

Bottleneck characterization:
- Compute vs memory: attention matmul is compute-heavy but register-limited (reduces occupancy). Softmax/reduction kernels are memory-bound. So there's a split: some kernels suffer from low occupancy (register/shared-memory constraints), others from DRAM bandwidth.
- Launch overhead: many small kernels create measurable host overhead. This is reduced significantly by CUDA Graphs.
- Fragmentation due to dynamic sequence lengths: smaller sequences (<=128) create many small kernels and underutilize SMs.

Hypotheses and implications:
1) Lowering per-thread register usage in fused attention kernel (via refactor or using fewer temporaries) could increase occupancy and improve throughput for long sequences. Risk: may increase instruction count; need microbench.
2) Rebalance work between shared memory and registers: for some attention tiles, moving some scratch to shared memory (if it reduces register pressure) may help occupancy at cost of potential bank conflicts; experiment required.
3) Merge small kernels where possible (kernel fusion) or use persistent kernels to amortize launch cost -- CUDA Graphs helped already and should be extended to more of the hot loop.
4) Improve batching strategy for short seqs: dynamic micro-batching to increase effective SM utilization without hurting latency SLOs.
5) Investigate quantization / Tensor Core paths (AMP + wmma) for matmul kernels to shift more work to Tensor Cores and raise effective throughput.

Quick win checklist (priority ordered):
- [P0] Extend CUDA Graph coverage to include kv-cache update + attention loop (owner: Ravi) -- expected +8-12% SM utilization improvement. Ticket: JIRA-INFR-4321.
- [P0] Add Nsight Compute reg-usage traces for attention fused kernel across two compile variants (current and reduced-temporary) and compare achieved_occupancy (owner: Avery).
- [P1] Implement small-kernel coalescing for kv-cache copies (owner: Sofia) -- aim to reduce number of kernel launches by 60% for seq<=128.
- [P1] Prototype shared-memory refactor for attention tile to trade registers for shared mem, measure latency and occupancy (owner: Liam).
- [P2] Micro-batching experiment for low-latency mode: measure latency P50/P99 tradeoffs at bs=2..8.

Data captures / artifacts (where to find traces):
- Nsight Systems traces: s3://redwood-profiles/nsight/2026-02/nsight_run_20260225.qdrep
- Nsight Compute reports: s3://redwood-profiles/nsight-cu/2026-02/attn_fused_variant_1.ncu-rep
- Lightweight profiler snapshots: /tmp/prof/2026-02-attn-profile.json (on test host vm)

Open questions / next experiments:
- How much occupancy gain can we achieve before instruction throughput or register spill penalty negates gains? Need A/B microbench.
- Is there a stable, portable shared-memory layout that reduces register pressure across Ampere and Hopper?
- For private deployments with older cards (V100/RTX A6000), does CUDA Graphs provide same relative improvement? Run targeted tests.

Notes to reviewer:
- This doc is a working capture of runs; not all Nsight reports attached here (too large). I checked that the CUDA Graph prototype branch in the repo (PR #978) contains the reproducer and measured gains locally.
- Expect follow-up PRs for the CUDA Graph expansion and a Nsight Compute micro-report comparing reg usage across variants.
